svg.text: Total section A-A · grid B
through the east and west buttresses, looking north
Footing 1800 x 250, underside at -1000 (frost depth
and bearing are guesses).
Printed wall 400, same pattern as the roof: two 80
inner layers, a 160 air zone, an 80 outer layer.
Solid base of the roof: the first 300 (vertical)
above the eave is completely solid concrete, 400
wide, no air zone; there is no ring beam.
Buttress 400 wide, 1000 from the inner face (600
beyond the wall), one about every 1.5 m (8 per
side); it rises to +2.50, flush with the roof base.
Roof shell: 400 thick square to the slope at the
base (two 80 inner layers, a 160 air zone, an 80
outer layer), 320 at the crown; about 500 / 400
horizontally.
Crown opening 1000 clear; roof rises 6000 over 4500,
slope 53.1° (36.9° from the vertical).
Everything is 3D printed in 10 mm layers; crossed
hatch = solid cast concrete (roof base, ribs).
Printed layer joints and the cast fill of the
buttress and footing are shown in the roof-grid
sheets and in detail D1.
Outside the printed shell: insulation 100 (dotted),
then the outer layer (cladding 30, dark).
Cast ribs of the roof grid, seen on the back face as
dashed outlines (roof grid B, diamond lattice). The
cut lies in the air zone between ribs; rib sections
are on the roof-grid sheets.
from your sketches
assumed by me, to confirm
Notes
Layer pattern from your drawing; at the crown the second
inner layer ends, so the leaf is 80 there (assumed).
The cut runs through the 4th buttress from the south (y =
-743); the north wall with its door and windows is seen
beyond.
Faint grid on the back roof face and the north wall =
printed pieces in running bond, about 1500 wide (assumed
sizes). Dashed outlines on the back roof face = cast ribs.
